Synopsis:
STATE NODES - first half of dialogue, Thulla is in EXTREME pain, speaking in short, terse sentences.Second half - she's weary but recovering.Thulla is a member of the Ironhand Gnomes, a group of militant gnomish artificers who came to the Underdark to find a forbidden - and extremely secret - formula for runepowder: an explosive of awesome power.Thulla is a true believer in the cause - when her group was captured by duergar, she escaped but picked up a poisoned wound on the way. She's slowly succumbing to poison - initially vague and feverish. If we heal her, she's exhausted but straight back on task, giving us the job of freeing her people.

Cluster Contexts:
- UND_MyconidCircle_InjuredGnome.json: Thulla is an Ironhand gnome artificer who escaped duergar captivity but picked up a slowly fatal Underdark poison; at the start of the scene she’s in extreme pain and speaks in short, terse lines, later growing weary but lucid if healed. She’s distrustful of strangers and warns against rifling through her things — the narration suggests an antidote exists but is likely held by her captors or the poisoner. Off‑screen, Derryth Bonecloak (a gruff dwarven alchemist from Baldur’s Gate) is nearby tending injured gnomes and is the most likely source of medical aid, though she is motivated by profit and affected by Baelen’s circumstance, so what the player already has or offers (noblestalk, Misty Step scroll, payment, prior deals with myconids) will shape options. If cured, Thulla will be exhausted but immediately return to the mission: freeing her people and pursuing the forbidden runepowder formula.
- DEN_General_TieflingGuard5.json: She drank a potion given to her by the hag, with the promise that it would make her strong as steel. It did, but it has paralysed her legs. The effects are temporary, but she's angry and embarassed at the situation she's found herself. She doesn't suspect any foul play on the hag's part. We get a clue about this mysterious old woman selling potions in the cave, and through tagged gameplay can reveal that she's been duped. She is frustrated at herself - she wanted to help in the goblin fight, and instead she is sprawled on the ground.
- DEN_Apprentice_Cyanide.json: Nettie leads the player into a lab and fetches a thorn. The player doesn't know, but the thorn is a deadly poison. Nettie knows it's the only choice she has - the player could transform into a monster and kill everyone in the camp. She sees this as a kindness - the transformation is terrible - so she has a very 'matter of fact nurse' tone about the whole thing before she scratches you, but will get stressed if you resist. Once she's scratched the player, her tone will be softer - kinder. She plans to sit with you while you pass and make it as easy as possible. The player will have to convince her they're not a threat if they're going to get the antidote. She'll be slow to convince, hesitant to allow any risk to the camp. Nettie is STANDING for this entire dialog.
- UND_NGB_InjuredGnome_ThullaMurder.json: Myconid responses to seeing Thulla - the injured gnome - being killed through the dialog.
- UND_TheDrowNere_Mutiny.json: Dialogue after you destroy the cave-in and set Nere free. Thrinn has been put in charge of getting Nere out, but it's the player who accomplishes it. Nere almost just died from inhaling poisonous gas, so he's very angry. In this dialogue, you determine the fate of the gnomes as well as Nere and the mutinous duergar.

context: Thulla is an Ironhand gnome artificer who escaped duergar captivity but sustained a slowly fatal Underdark poison and starts the scene in extreme pain, speaking in short, terse sentences; if healed she will be weary but quickly lucid. She’s a true believer in rescuing her captured kin and the forbidden runepowder formula, and she’s deeply distrustful of strangers—warning anyone not to rifle through her things. Off‑screen, an antidote almost certainly exists but is likely held by her captors or the poisoner, and Derryth Bonecloak, a nearby dwarven alchemist, is the most likely source of medical aid (and is motivated by profit), so what the player offers or brings will shape options. The narration supports attempts to search her belongings (players may find little of value), and if cured Thulla will be exhausted but immediately insist on getting back to freeing her people.
